text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Planned changes to relations between insurers Sampo, Elake-Varma and Yrittajain Fennia will be postponed over summer.
- Finnish companies have vague knowledge of EU's subsidies and have not applied for enough support, survey by Central Chamber of Commerce shows.

- Finance Minister Sauli Niinsto to decide alone on design of Finnish euro coins in the near future; both the pan-European face of the coin and the Finnish face are to be presented at EU's Amsterdam summit in June.
- Finnish MPs speaking in parliament oppose plans to merge the European Union (EU) with the military alliance Western European Union (WEU).
- No referendum is needed for Finland to join EMU, President Martti Ahtisaari says.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen named environment minister Pekka Haavisto head of a ministerial group handling controversial Natura 2000 scheme for environmental protection.
- Finns are satisfied with educational system and do not want longer school days, study shows.
- Social benefit fraud increased in Helsinki.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Forestry stocks have jumped from a cyclical downturn to the list of analysts' favourite stocks.

- Indian and Pakistani bed linen makers have rapidly increased market share in Finland at the expense of domestic producers; European Commission fears dumping in EU and proposes tolls for imports from these countries.

- A hoax bid for Turku telephone company Turun Puhelin, possibly from an Internet "hacker-rascal", delays sale of the company; investment banker fears this sort of hoaxing may increase when information is public and easily available.
- Finnish retailers expect clear growth, EU survey shows.
- Banking group Merita's life insurance arm says current strong growth in life insurance saving in Finland is only the beginning.
AAMULEHTI
- Police to get wider authorities in fighting money laundering, interior ministry proposes.
- Many sweets and spices contain illegal additives, inspection shows.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Traffic minister Matti Aura wants to maintain licence funding for the national broadcasting company YLE.
- Market demands have made the chemical industry aware of the environment.
DEMARI

- UN human rights envoy to former Yugoslavia Elisabeth Rehn, who lost the final round of Finland's presidential election in 1994 to Martti Ahtisaari, says her current job is more important than the President's.
- City of Helsinki is planning a 90 million markka swimming stadium.
